correctness.rationale: For p>=7 the constrained gradient cubic forces all coordinates into either three distinct values with multiplicities (2,2,2), or into fifteen two-versus-four points. This exhausts the geometric reduced singular locus and proves the line–point incidence. Normalization is disjoint union of 15 genus-zero line components, and the exact point identity #Sigma=#N-#B+#P gives the displayed zeta formula. A stdlib verifier exhaustively enumerated all 720 permutations and all eleven partition spectra, checked fixed-point agreement for each power 1–12, and directly enumerated the projective gradient equations over F7 and F11 (90,150 singular points). Finite-field samples are checks, not the all-fields proof. Limits: nonreduced scheme and p<7 not included.

value.rationale: The distinguished reduced singular curve of the trace Igusa quartic is a natural nonnormal projective curve with 15 components and 15 triple points. Its full zeta over every finite field of characteristic at least 7 and every sextic étale twisting type is calculated, including all 11 Frobenius orbit spectra of its normalization, singular points and branches. In one type there are three rational triple points but no rational irreducible line; another has no rational points at all. Computing a positive-dimensional arithmetic invariant and the normalization gluing makes this more than repackaging a finite permutation table; it does not claim ambient-threefold zeta.
